assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only peach-girl:adachi-momo@manga#second-pass-character-monograph (PEACH_GIRL_MOMO_MONOGRAPH.md, version 1.1, active_provisional) and peach-girl:adachi-momo@manga#time-indexed-literary-dossier (PEACH_GIRL_MOMO_TIME_INDEXED_RECONSTRUCTION_DOSSIER.md, version 1.0, active_provisional) at basis_commit, read in full as reviewed repository analysis of the original Japanese 新装版 manga V01-V18. The Peach Girl current-state and corpus map was read for method, authority order and scope only. The volume readings, the four longitudinal ledgers, the second-pass reconciliation, coverage and reconstruction reassessments, the G4 rules, cases, results and runner, and the other characters' monographs and dossiers are not curated evidence on this subject and nothing is borrowed from them. The project's BOUNDED_PROVISIONAL, PASS_SCOPED and BLOCKED_NO_HELD_OUT_VALIDATION labels are inputs, not conclusions. No anime, live-action or sequel material is included, and the evaluator performed no primary-source inspection.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Fourteen dossier states from M01 (V01 i0178) through M14 (V18 i0178), each excluding later or unreceived information, together with the monograph's V01-V18 developmental account. No default state is designated for an unspecified request, so a cutoff must be named. Anything after the V18 ending, including future safety, durable repair and the course of the final relationship, is expressly unestablished, and no in-world calendar dates are fixed.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph states a governing reading (Momo Adachi's development concerns authority over the interpretation of her own life: visible before she is known, then repeatedly overridden by appearances, rival accounts, photographs and her own earlier declarations) and tests it against located counterreadings (the forged crisis and spectacular rescue at the end; every Tōji feeling as denial, rejected). The dossier lists competing goals and actual alternatives per state (M02: protect herself from renewed disbelief, keep love, recover swimming; M09: allow Kairi Okayasu a real decision, preserve a stopping condition). This is specialist literary interpretation. Neither artifact gives conditional decision rules, and the dossier forbids exact motivational weights, a forgiveness threshold or a diagnosis, so B is not supported.

The dossier's exact endpoint index gives fourteen states at image-level cutoffs (M01 V01 i0178 to M14 V18 i0178), each with an accessible-state summary, the meaningful change and a required exclusion, for example M07 still-love at V11 versus the V12 more-love comparison, and M09 retaining Jigorō's V13 participant denial while Kairi's influenza and location stay unknown. The monograph orders the same development (declined restart in V03, revenge reversal in V07, the second-for-now offer in V12 and its cost in V13, the explicit Tōji choice at V17_164 and V18_6-7, the Kairi declaration at V18 i0143 before the rescue). A is not supported: the eleven retrieval vectors are unexecuted, both artifacts are active_provisional from the same second-pass authorship, and V05-V06, V10 and V13 have no dedicated state card.

The evidence analyzes written interaction by communication type: spoken question, private caption, remembered speech, report and inference are separated; V11's narrowing questions and V12's comparison elicit different answers; V14 i0076 keeps the surname address Okayasu while setting the noon-plus-five-minutes condition; at V15 i0071-i0072 a spoken fragment is distinguished from the fully private question. Japanese wording is rarely quoted beyond 外見 and 見た目, and both artifacts disclaim acoustic delivery, a global address transition, an all-situation script and generated canonical dialogue. This supports bounded questions about what Momo did or did not say to whom, not a register model.

Ordinary domains are located: swimming and the damaged suit (V03), study and exams, affordable dates, apology cookies, the L-sign practice and birthday (V04-V05), the crocheted case with yarn bought at a craft shop (V09-V10), and part-time work and shift scheduling (V15). The monograph says these domains give choices weight but cannot establish relational safety, and the dossier treats them as evidence rather than decoration. They are listed within crisis-centred readings rather than modeled as routines, and no domestic, family or noncrisis daily pattern is described.

Relations are differentiated by person and state: Kazuya Tojigamori, called Tōji (wordless approach refused at M01; declined restart at M02; renewed dating and the L code at M03; respect for a stop as safety at M10; the V18 hotel conflict); Kairi Okayasu (uncertain company at M05, public dating at M06, his stop and continued Misao attachment at M07, the informed second-for-now offer and her collar-grab pressure at M08, finite waiting at M09); Sae Kashiwagi (an ordinary friendship origin, rescue without forgiveness at M04, the counsel she originates at V18 i0140). The evidence is centred on these three; Misao, Kyo and Momo's family appear only as information sources, and no recipient-register table or matched-recipient rule is given.

Both artifacts separate panel-accessible private text from what partners receive (the V15 private question, V13 private admission that second place is not enough, V18_18's revision of her earlier self-presentation) and refuse to install later corrections in earlier minds (the V13 Jigorō account cannot remove V06 distress; Ryo's bodily-response theory is not a verified cause). Interior claims stay tied to captions and focalization. The dossier forbids exact motivational weights and abstains where no caption exists (the V18 phone-struggle conclusion), so a demonstrated interior model is not supported.

Located conflict conduct includes the slap of Sae and refusal of blanket blame (V03), participation in and then reversal of mirrored punishment, entry and resistance and receiving Sae's slap (V07), binding Kairi's wrists and dragging him (V02), the pool kick at a known water fear (V09), the collar grab and kiss after Kairi's no (V12_149-154), the gift throw under partial information (V09), and rejecting Kairi's declaration (V18). The monograph treats these as situated fallibility rather than a type. No general conflict policy or escalation rule is stated, and outcomes beyond V18 are unestablished.

The monograph separates rescue from forgiveness (V07 and V13), informed offers from the other participant's assent (V12), and desire from permission within an encounter (V05), and it denies that Momo's heroine status makes her pressure emancipatory. These are the analyst's ethical distinctions about Momo's acts; the evidence shows few deliberations from her own perspective, and the dossier abstains on any forgiveness threshold. Substantial interpretation without a deliberation procedure.

The evidence mentions friendly irritation, comic retaliation (the pool kick) and humor among situated speech functions without describing a humor or play repertoire. This gap says nothing about Momo's actual humor.

Both artifacts cover V01-V18 with image-coordinate locators and route their provenance to all-18 source-first receipts by four named readers, the dated reconciliation and the audited V01-V04 inheritance. The monograph is analytical prose, not primary-image inspection; the evaluator could not recheck the receipt register, ledgers or readings, which are outside the set; and both artifacts disclose that the second pass was authored and integrated within the project with owner acceptance pending. B is not supported.

Affirmative limits and corrections are located: the declined restart against an expected reunion (V03), Momo's own coercive pressure (V02 binding and dragging, V09 kick, V12 collar grab), the withdrawn inference of a completed V15 night (corrected by V18 i0116-i0117), the narrowed V18 phone-scene misreading, the denial that Sae's body-honest wording is Momo's authorship, and the rule that rescue breaths do not settle the old CPR dispute. Both artifacts close sections with explicit abstentions. Each case is documented within these two same-authored artifacts and is not independently validated; there is no counterexample audit table.

Every state has an inclusive image cutoff and an exclusion, and the dossier states that a later auditor correction can identify an exclusion but cannot become earlier character knowledge. Communication type and receipt are timed (V14 i0040-i0042 heard despite later forgetting; the V15 i0071/i0072 split; Tōji gone before V16 i0159). A is not supported: no default state is designated, in-world dates are not fixed, and the retrieval vectors that would test the cutoffs are unexecuted.

scenario_readiness.note: Both artifacts disclaim acoustic delivery, an all-context script and generated canonical dialogue, and the dossier forbids forcing a global address change. Lines written for Momo beyond the few situated forms analyzed would be fluent invention rather than source-supported voice. This bounds the evidence set, not Momo's actual speech.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: Any named dossier state M01-M14 or V01-V18 cutoff; no post-V18 state.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Any counterpart, including Tōji, Kairi and Sae as the evidence describes them at the named cutoff; the refusal does not depend on the partner.
setting_constraints: Crossover, counterfactual or materially novel contexts outside the canon cutoffs
Adult independent work, politics, parenting or unfamiliar clinical crises
Behavioral or dialogue simulation rather than retrieval of a canon state

scenario_readiness.note: The dossier states that adult independent work, politics, parenting, unfamiliar clinical crises and crossover contexts lack adequate source coverage, and its vector M-R11 requires abstention on scenario portability. Its states are retrieval cards for canon cutoffs, not a basis for a materially novel context.

Ordinary school, sport, gift and work domains are located, but only as context for crisis-centred states; no baseline for an unfamiliar ordinary scene is given. Bounded canon questions about these located episodes remain answerable.

The dossier abstains on a forgiveness threshold and on exact motivational weights, and the monograph's ethical distinctions are analyses of completed acts. No procedure for a new ethical choice can be run on this evidence set.

conditions: A dossier state M01-M14 or an equally exact V01-V18 cutoff is named; no default state is assumed and no information after the cutoff or unreceived by Momo is used.
The partner is Kazuya Tojigamori (Tōji) or Kairi Okayasu as the evidence describes him at that cutoff; Sae Kashiwagi appears only in roles the evidence locates.
Output is a description of Momo's accessible state, goals, alternatives and constraints, with the dossier's abstentions kept; no quoted dialogue is produced as canon.
Later responsive contact never supplies earlier permission, and an informed offer is never treated as the other participant's assent.
No outcome after V18, durable repair, future safety or exclusive arrangement not depicted at the cutoff is asserted.
scenario_readiness.note: The evidence set is built around the two romances and supplies, for each named state, Momo's accessible knowledge, competing goals, actual choices and exclusions. Readiness is conditional because the use supported is retrieval and bounded description at a canon cutoff, not prediction of a new romantic outcome; the project's own retrieval vectors are unexecuted and its operational acceptance is blocked.
Her work is a V15 part-time job with shift scheduling, and the dossier lists adult independent work as lacking adequate coverage. No workplace behavior beyond the located episodes can be supported.

known_limits.statement: The dossier describes its fourteen states as literary reconstruction states, not an executable model, new observation IDs or replacement freezes; the monograph claims no operational reconstruction.

The dossier's eleven retrieval vectors were designed after source outcomes were known and are unexecuted consistency questions, not runner executions or held-out probes; operational acceptance is BLOCKED_NO_HELD_OUT_VALIDATION and no predictive accuracy or calibration is claimed.

A later account (the V13 Jigorō denial, V18 disclosures, later responsive contact) cannot be installed in an earlier state of Momo's knowledge or used as earlier permission; each state excludes later or unreceived information.
No acoustic delivery, global address transition, all-context catchphrase or generated canonical dialogue is supported; at V14 i0076 Momo still uses Okayasu.

Adult independent work, politics, parenting, unfamiliar clinical crises and crossover contexts lack adequate source coverage; no diagnosis, forgiveness threshold or exact motivational weights may be invented.
Both artifacts carry SECOND_PASS_SCOPED_SEMANTIC_REVIEW_PASSED_OWNER_ACCEPTANCE_PENDING, were authored and accepted within the project's own second pass, and are active_provisional.

The volume readings, four ledgers, source receipts, reconciliation, coverage and reconstruction reassessments and the G4 rules, cases and results are not curated evidence on this subject, so their warrants and the project's preserved probe failures were not rechecked here. Missing support is not evidence of absence.
